senses.gloss:
एन एन, a pronom. base (used for certain
cases of the 3rd personal pronoun, and occurring only
in the acc. sing. du. pl. (एनम्, एनाम्, एनद्, &c.),
inst. sing. (एनेन, एनया), gen. loc. du. (एनयोस्, Ved.
एनोस्); the other cases are formed fr. the pronom.
base अ, see under इदम्), he, she, it; this, that.
This pronoun is enclitic and cannot begin a sentence.
It is generally used alone, so that एनम् पुरुषम्,
‘that man,’ would be very unusual if not incorrect.
Grammarians assert that the substitution of एनम्
for इमम् or एतम् takes place in case of the re-em-
ployment of these pronouns in the subsequent part
of a sentence; see Gram. 836; [cf. Gr. ἕν, οἶος
Goth. ains; Old Pruss. ains; Lat oinos, unus.]

एनस् एनस्, अस्, n. (fr. इन्, but said to be
fr. rt. 5. इ), mischief, crime; curse, unhappiness; sin,
offence, fault; censure, blame.
—एनस्-वत्, आन्, अती,
अत्, or एनस्-विन्, ई, इनी, इ, wicked, sinful, a sinner.

एनस्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. caused by crime; sinful,
wicked, wrong.
